assertion: The external plugin contract defines pinned identity, dependency closure, host invocation, activation lifetime, input/result envelopes and existing-operation hook names. The contract preserves standalone resources, core authorization and acceptance boundaries, offline composition and guarded resume semantics. Workflow-changing choices and unresolved host limitations are explicitly routed to the owner workflow decision task. Project defaults, explicit temporary run overrides and frozen effective configuration are defined separately from installed-package state; confirmed installation enables only the exact displayed hooks and readiness effects.
limitations: Contract design only; lifecycle, composition, invocation and comparative qualification remain separate implementation tasks.
observations: Pinned resources, license/dependency closure and native requirements have explicit owned identity.
All existing-operation phases preserve complete core operations and locked selection/check/authorization invariants.
Project installation confirmation binds exact enabled settings; acquisition, skill execution and frozen effective run configuration remain separate.
Codex-first source-backed bounded adapter is distinct from native execution and universal support; unsupported tools return prerequisites.
Question/findings/failure envelopes, idempotent attempts, stale-result guards and ordinary authorized rework are specified.
New stages and remaining material policy decisions route to actual owner discussion; recommendation efficacy remains unqualified until comparison.
reviewer: Root source inspection and independent read-only review_plugin_planning_commit
